thread:
maria: FYI customer xyz-prod reporting sudden spikes in API errors + 500s after a failover yesterday. They say traffic got routed to us-east unexpectedly and p99 jumped to ~720ms.

jordan: Can you paste the original customer report and the region header they saw?

maria: Quote from ticket: "We hit a string of 502/504s around 13:12 UTC and our logs show requests hitting us-east-1 when our app is pinned to eu-west-1. Heartbeat checks looked green for eu-west before the switch." They attached this probe log snippet: 
```
[2025-09-21T13:11:45Z] probe/eu-west-1: alive=1 ttl=30 rtt=12ms
[2025-09-21T13:11:52Z] probe/eu-west-1: alive=0 ttl=0 rtt=NA
[2025-09-21T13:11:55Z] routing: fallback -> us-east-1 (policy: latency_threshold)
[2025-09-21T13:12:01Z] probe/eu-west-1: alive=1 ttl=28 rtt=14ms
```
maria: Customer claims the health probe flapped to 0 for ~3s which triggered routing to us-east. They also saw a mismatch between probe agent IP + the edge node mapping.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20250921-97 (severity: P2) - assigned to eng-sre oncall.

erica: Thanks, digging in. Two quick asks: 1) can we get the raw probe traces from the eu-west health agents around that window? 2) did the autoscaler / control plane log any region-level capacity events?

jordan: Pulling probe traces now. Early suspicion: probe TTL mis-parse when the upstream NAT rotates ephemeral IPs — health agent treats response as coming from different probe target and drops it. That yields a transient false negative.

maria: Customer says their networking team rotated a firewall rule around 13:10 to remove an old IP. Might align.

erica: I see repeated NAT churn in edge logs: `edge-proxy-12` saw source IP change for probe stream at 13:11:52, which matches the drop. Routing policy has a 2sdebounce but the failover was allowed because we had three lost probes in the sample window.

jordan: Repro plan: try simulating ephemeral IP rotation for the health agent to verify false negative behavior. Quick repro steps for support/customer:
```
# simulate probe response then change source IP
curl -H "X-Probe-Id: eu-west-1" https://probe-api.internal/health
# on a second host rotate NAT or modify source
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source 3.3.3.3
# re-run probe -> check controller logs
```
maria: Can we provide a mitigation for the customer while we fix the parsing? They want to avoid future cross-region failovers.

erica: Short term: increase probe sample window and raise debounce threshold for eu regions for this customer: `routing.failover.debounce_ms=5000` and `health.probe.sample_size=7` (requires redeploy of config to their tenant). That will make us less sensitive to 1-3s NAT churn.

jordan: Longer term: update probe identity verification — include an HMACed probe token so agent can verify continuity across ephemeral IP rotation. Also update controller logic to consider stable agent IDs not just source IP.

oncall-bot: Patch request opened: PR-2341 -> eng-platform (target: 2025-09-28)

maria: Customer accepted the band-aid (increase debounce) and asked for repro steps so they can test on staging. Sending them the curl/snippet.

erica: I pushed a temporary override for xyz-prod that reduces failover sensitivity at 13:45 UTC. Monitoring now.

jordan: Follow-ups: (1) add unit test for probe parser with NAT rotation cases, (2) instrument probe traces with agent-id in routing decisions, (3) postmortem once root cause confirmed.

maria: Thanks team. I'll update ticket and close the loop with the customer once we confirm stability. :white_check_mark:

customer-ops: Quick note from customer: after the override we stayed in eu-west and p99 dropped back to ~98ms. Will run longer soak tomorrow. Thanks! :tada:
